latest_final: Kameda and Umio were political rivals. Kameda was cremated, leaving his bones fragmented, while Umio was buried with his bones intact. Umio’s burial was less prestigious and was carried out by the faction that defeated him. People therefore took the difference in funerary treatment as evidence that Umio had lost their political struggle, despite Kameda’s more visibly damaged remains.
